## Summary

Five tasks (T-1095–T-1099) shipped in one stacked train hardening the loop's
own trust boundary: a self-triggered means-ends reflection norm (T-1095), the
tamper-resistance criticality rule plus two selection-trust gates it decides
(T-1096), a `--trial-branch` flag closing a git-safety gap in `team-init.sh`
(T-1097), an end-to-end fixture suite executing the shipped trial-adoption
recipe (T-1098), and a duplicate-`## Done`-heading class-check CI-wired
against this repository's own board (T-1099). All five landed with both
gates green; zero pre-commitment drops executed; one human intervention
(an operator-held pause condition at T-1095, not a drop). The cycle's
own shipped gates (`check-entry-mode.sh`, `check-spec-review.sh`) went live
mid-sprint and caught a real cross-writer collision on their first firing.

## Drop review (mandatory this cycle)

**Zero pre-commitment drops were executed across all five tasks.** No
Droppable disposition fired; no pre-priced drop-order component was
discarded. Two approaches came close enough to be worth naming, plus one
distinct human-held gate that is not a drop at all:

- **T-1096 delivered-change review, round 2**: a new Blocker landed
  (`skills/run/SKILL.md:45` hardcoded a `bin/`-prefixed invocation that
  breaks under the plugin's real deployment shape). The pre-commitment's
  factual trigger is "two consecutive review rounds landing an
  *independently-new* Blocker/Major against the same component." It did
  **not** fire: the orchestrator classified this Blocker as a *propagation
  gap* introduced by round 1's own M1 fix, not an independently-new defeat
  of §3's design — the same classification logic T-1095 shipped this
  sprint, applied live for its second time in the same cycle. Source:
  `.shell-team/todo.md` T-1096 entry, sub-bullet beginning "**means-ends
  reflection (T-1095), applied to this firing**"; `.shell-team/reviews/T-1096.md`
  round-2 section.
- **T-1099 delivered-change review, round 1**: a Blocker (empty-identity
  duplicate-heading false-negative) plus a Major (internal-tab truncation)
  landed against the same component (`bin/check-entry-mode.sh`'s duplicate
  judgment — actually `check-board-headings.sh`'s awk pass). Both closed in
  a single rework round as one class (re-encoded identity). No *second*
  round landed a new independently-new Blocker/Major against that same
  component, so the two-consecutive-round trigger never had a chance to
  fire — one round of findings does not arm it. Source: `.shell-team/todo.md`
  T-1099 entry (delivered-change review trail sub-bullet);
  `.shell-team/reviews/T-1099.md`.
- **Not a drop, for the record**: T-1095's operator-imposed pause ("if the
  cross-provider review does not `APPROVE` on its first round, the loop
  stops there rather than entering rework on its own authority") is a
  **human-held gate**, not the loop's own pre-commitment/disposition
  mechanism — it produced a `GO` on a rework proposal, not a drop of any
  scope. Source: `.shell-team/interventions/T-1095.md`.

## Keep — what worked

- **Full-closure discipline paid off measurably, twice.** T-1097's QA first
  ran a partial (44/102) blast-radius sweep, then completed it to 102/102 on
  orchestrator instruction — finding the T-1096 `AC15` step-count flip only
  the completed sweep could see. T-1099's QA substituted a mechanically-scoped
  pass first, then completed it to the full 104/104 population under the same
  obligation and found **four** additional flips (T-1087 AC8, T-1088 AC6,
  T-1089 AC10, T-1090 AC6 — predecessor zero-deletion board locks defeated by
  an indirection class, run-time path resolution, invisible to byte-level
  scoping) that the scoped pass missed entirely. The obligation's yield is now
  a measured number, not an argued one. Source: `.shell-team/todo.md` T-1097
  QA round-2 entry ("Blast radius" full-population note) and T-1099 entry,
  sub-bullet "full-population sweep completion note (orchestrator)".
- **The sprint's own shipped gates went live within the sprint and caught a
  real defect on first exercise.** `check-entry-mode.sh` fired at T-1097's,
  T-1098's and T-1099's freeze seams; at T-1098 it produced its **first live
  refusal** — a genuine two-writer dispatch-transcription collision between
  `pm-spec` and the orchestrator — and at T-1099 `pm-spec` spontaneously
  withheld the dispatch transcription, citing T-1098's collision, with no
  instruction to do so: discipline propagating without being told. Source:
  `.shell-team/todo.md` T-1098 entry ("freeze sweep (2026-08-25, coordinating
  session)" sub-bullet) and T-1099 entry (same-named sub-bullet).
- **Freeze sweeps caught two instrument-defect classes before they could
  byte-lock a false criterion.** T-1096: a wrapped-phrase single-line grep
  (missed a sentence hard-wrapped across two lines) and an assignment-line
  row count, both repaired before the intent hash was recorded. T-1098: an
  undefined "flag-span" term (ambiguity in the spec, not the measurement) and
  a `## Blast radius` reproduce line missing `export B F` that silently
  derived a **vacuous zero-item** population — `AC17` would have locked that
  empty block byte-for-byte had the sweep not caught it; `AC17` was then
  hardened with three value-independent non-vacuity assertions. Source:
  `.shell-team/todo.md` T-1096 entry ("freeze sweep (2026-08-24...)" and
  `.shell-team/specs/T-1096-selection-trust-gates.md:365`); T-1098 entry,
  "pre-freeze correction 2" sub-bullet.
- **A self-monitoring re-evaluation trigger fired exactly as designed, and
  was recorded rather than silently passed.**
  `docs/loop-engineering/record-tamper-resistance.md`'s own re-evaluation
  trigger ("the promotion of a third obligation into arm A") fired at T-1099
  and is recorded both in the doc itself and on the board entry, explicitly

  `.shell-team/todo.md` T-1099 entry, `tamper-arm-rule-v1` sub-bullet.
- **The means-ends reflection norm this cycle shipped (T-1095) was applied to
  its own cycle, live, more than once.** T-1096's round-2 classification

<!-- retro-section: problem -->
## Problem — what hurt

- **The verify-axis dispatch decision was split incorrectly across four
  consecutive tasks, and this was only surfaced by an operator question, not
  by the loop's own reflection.** T-1096's, T-1097's, T-1098's and T-1099's
  `dispatch: verify` records each priced fan-out against the *fixture-suite*
  population only (small, sequential, shares one temp root) and concluded
  `serial` — correctly, for that half. None of the four records separately
  evaluated the *mechanism-class full-population two-arm diff* (the same
  tier1-fanout mechanism T-1095 itself measured a **43.84%** wall-clock
  saving on, in this very cycle) against its own, much larger population
  (101–104 specs × 2 arms). That work stayed serial for three consecutive
  tasks and cost real wall-clock time: T-1098's QA ran roughly 3.2 hours with
  two stalls, one of them a background-tooling stall diagnosed mid-session
  after "no further progress for over an hour of wall-clock time." Source:
  `.shell-team/todo.md` T-1096 entry ("dispatch: verify — serial..."), T-1097
  entry (same), T-1098 entry (same, plus "Risk notes for reviewer" item 4 —
  the background-tooling stall); `.shell-team/runs/t1098-routing-map.md:42`;
  orchestrator briefing (2026-08-26), item 2 (the analysis itself — including
  the framing that this split should be evaluated per-work-type rather than
  per-task — reached the record only because the operator asked
  「今回のQAは分割できなかった？」on 2026-08-25; it was not autonomously
  surfaced by any task's own freeze sweep, QA verdict, or review round).
- **Hand-derived quantity claims in prose caused a real QA round to fail, and
  recurred across two different tasks in the same cycle.** T-1095's QA round
  1 `FAIL`ed on two narrative miscounts in the spec's own `## Summarized
  sources` prose (a registry-row count stated as 6, measured as 5; a line
  count stated as 33, measured as 32 — the 33 traced to reading a file
  reader's last displayed row number as a line count). T-1096's freeze sweep
  separately caught and retracted a hand-derived "working tree: 1" count in
  its own count-premise table, explicitly noting it was "hand-derived from a
  read, not produced by the stated command." Both are instances of the
  corpus's already-promoted 2026-08-24 lesson (quantity-claim defect risk
  tracks exposure to writing raw numeric literals, not role identity) —
  see Lesson candidates below for the disposition (extend, not duplicate).
  Source: `.shell-team/todo.md` T-1095 QA round-1 entry (2026-08-24,
  `qa-verifier`, "Failure — mandatory Summarized-sources check..." sub-bullet);
  `.shell-team/specs/T-1096-selection-trust-gates.md:365`.
- **The untracked-subagent-background class recurred roughly five times
  across QA/review agents this cycle despite standing foreground
  instructions**, per the orchestrator's own briefing — the same class the
  corpus's existing lesson (`feedback_subagent-background-not-tracked.md`)
  and `CLAUDE.local.md`'s watchdog discipline already name. Recurrence at
  this rate inside a single cycle, after the pattern is already named,
  suggests the existing mitigation is necessary but not sufficient. Source:
  orchestrator briefing (2026-08-26), item 8 (session-level detail, not
  independently visible in committed board text for this retro).
- **A machine-local session path with a username and session UUID reached a
  frozen spec's citation prose before review caught it.** T-1098's spec cited
  a scratchpad path of that shape in `## Summarized sources`; the cross-provider
  review's round-1 Major closed it (fixed to the `.shell-team/runs/`
  convention), and the reviewer additionally self-corrected its own record's
  verbatim quote of the leaked path in the same edit. The sweep found it was
  the only tracked instance this cycle — a real hygiene gap, caught once, not
  yet caught at authoring time. Source: `.shell-team/todo.md` T-1098 entry,
  "delivered-change review trail" sub-bullet.

<!-- retro-section: try -->
## Try — what to change next cycle

- **Split the verify-axis dispatch decision by work type, not by task.** When
  a task's own verification duty includes both fixture-suite work and a
  mechanism-class full-population diff, `pm-spec`'s `dispatch: verify` record
  should price and elect each half independently rather than writing one
  `serial`/`tier1-fanout` line for the task as a whole — a task can correctly
  be `serial` on one axis and `tier1-fanout`-eligible on the other. Owning
  role: `pm-spec` (dispatch-grammar authoring); files:
  `docs/loop-engineering/phase-multiplexing.md` (the trigger text the
  dispatch line cites), `agents/pm-spec.md`. Expected improvement: recovers
  fan-out savings (T-1095 measured 43.84%) on the mechanism-class sweep for
  tasks like T-1096–T-1099 without changing the correct `serial` call on
  fixture-suite work. Source: orchestrator briefing item 2;
  `.shell-team/runs/t1098-routing-map.md:42`.
- **Add a lightweight, standing check to `pm-spec`'s `## Summarized sources`
  authoring step: any bare numeric literal describing a count, line number,
  or row tally gets a co-located `- reproduce:`/command form, or is flagged
  for the freeze sweep to independently re-derive before the hash is
  recorded** — rather than relying on the freeze sweep and QA to catch a
  hand-derived number after the fact each time. This is the already-promoted
  2026-08-24 lesson's "How to apply" clause, not yet mechanized into an
  authoring-time habit; two fresh instances this cycle (T-1095, T-1096) say
  the erosion the lesson names is still live. Owning role: `pm-spec`; files:
  `agents/pm-spec.md`, `.shell-team/lessons.md` (extend, do not duplicate —
  see Lesson candidates). Source: `.shell-team/lessons.md:1349-1357`.
- **Give the loop's own reflection a chance to surface a cross-task pattern
  like the verify-axis split without an operator question triggering it.**
  This cycle's own means-ends reflection (T-1095) is scoped to a single
  task's escalation firing points; nothing in the loop currently asks "does
  this task's dispatch decision repeat a pattern from the last N tasks in
  this train" at freeze or close-out time. A cheap version: `pm-spec`'s
  freeze sweep for task N in a stacked train skims the immediately preceding
  task's `dispatch:` lines for the same axis before writing its own. Owning
  role: `pm-spec`; files: `agents/pm-spec.md`. Source: orchestrator briefing
  item 2 (the observation this Try responds to).

## Lesson candidates

- `[common]` Extend the existing 2026-08-24 lesson ("Quantity-claim defect
  risk tracks a role's exposure to writing raw numeric literals, not the
  role's identity") rather than promoting a new entry: this cycle produced
  two fresh instances of the exact pattern the lesson already names (T-1095's
  registry/liveness-count QA FAIL; T-1096's retracted "working tree: 1"
  count), both in the same authoring role (`pm-spec`) writing prose counts
  by hand instead of deriving them from an embedded command. The lesson's
  "How to apply" clause is correct; what is missing is an authoring-time
  trigger, not a new rule. Source: `.shell-team/lessons.md:1349-1357`
  (existing entry); `.shell-team/todo.md` T-1095 QA round-1 entry;
  `.shell-team/specs/T-1096-selection-trust-gates.md:365`.
- `[target-specific]` When a task's own dispatch-grammar record elects
  `verify — serial` for a phase that bundles fixture-suite work with a
  mechanism-class full-population diff, split the election into two lines
  (one per work type) instead of one line covering both — a single `serial`
  election correctly priced against the smaller half silently carries the
  larger half's fan-out-eligible work along with it. **Source class:
  operator-question-triggered** — this pattern was not surfaced by any of
  the four affected tasks' own freeze sweeps, QA verdicts, or review rounds;
  it reached the record only because the operator asked
  「今回のQAは分割できなかった？」on 2026-08-25, after four tasks had already
  paid the cost. Source: orchestrator briefing (2026-08-26), item 2;
  `.shell-team/runs/t1098-routing-map.md:42`; `.shell-team/todo.md` T-1096/
  T-1097/T-1098/T-1099 entries' `dispatch: verify` sub-bullets. n/a for
  identifying detail (pattern and mechanism only).
- `[common]` A pre-commitment's classification call ("is this new-round
  finding an independently-new defeat, or a propagation gap from the
  previous round's own fix?") is itself a judgment worth writing down
  explicitly before deciding whether the two-consecutive-round trigger fires
  — this cycle exercised that exact call twice on the same task (T-1096
  round 2's spec-review Goal-sentence finding, then its delivered-change
  round 2's hardcoded-path Blocker) and both times the explicit written
  classification is what kept the trigger from mis-firing on a fix's own
  side effect. Generalizes beyond this repository: any loop with a
  two-consecutive-independent-finding trigger needs a named test for
  "independently new" vs. "caused by the previous fix," or the trigger both
  under- and over-fires. Source: `.shell-team/todo.md` T-1096 entry, both
  "orchestrator ruling" and "means-ends reflection (T-1095), applied to this
  firing" sub-bullets.
- `[target-specific]` A machine-local session path (username + session UUID
  shape) reached a frozen spec's `## Summarized sources` citation this
  cycle and was only caught by cross-provider review, not by authoring-time
  discipline or the freeze sweep. Consider adding a lightweight authoring-time
  self-check (or extending `bin/check-pii-shapes.sh`'s scope, if that is the
  right mechanical home) that flags a scratchpad-shaped absolute path in a
  spec's own prose before the freeze sweep runs, rather than relying on
  review to catch every instance. Source: `.shell-team/todo.md` T-1098 entry,
  "delivered-change review trail" sub-bullet.
